text:
noah: Noticing strange KMS egress from priv-cluster to 3.8.119.22 right after I tightened RBAC for secrets-manager. Could be a leak or a misroute. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: [ALERT] priv-cluster egress hit: 41 connections to 3.8.119.22 at 2026-04-10T08:12Z. source SA: secrets-manager.

anita: Oncall. Share the exact kubectl patch and which pods use secrets-manager SA. Run: `kubectl get pods -n control-plane -l app=secrets-writer -o name` and `kubectl get rolebinding -n control-plane`.

noah: Patch: `kubectl patch rolebinding controlplane-secrets -n control-plane --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/roleRef/name","value":"secrets-reader"}]'` at 08:10:40Z. Pods: secrets-writer-0 and secrets-writer-1.

dinesh: VPC logs show NAT-gw-1 used. I'm pulling pod env and /var/run/secrets. If token was cached in app memory it might retry. Suggest immediate token rotation + egress deny for 3.8.119.22.

clare: I'll prepare a rollback for the RBAC change and a short runbook addendum: require an egress smoke test after any secrets-role change.

maria: I'll start vuln-triage ticket and collect kube-apiserver audit, node journal, and our egress proxy logs. If KMS was invoked externally we need legal/compliance involved.

anita: Containment steps: 1) create ephemeral SA with no KMS access and patch deployment 2) delete SA tokens to force new tokens 3) cordon node if repeated 4) snapshot pod fs for forensics.

noah: Done: patched to temp-sa, restarted pods, applied VPC deny for 3.8.119.22. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-411 created. Assignees: anita, dinesh. Priority: P2.

clare: After-action items: add RBAC change gating, enforce short TTLs on SA tokens, and add automated alert for KMS host hits from private clusters.

noah: Thanks team. Will attach artifacts to the ticket and schedule a postmortem.
